extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, regulated entities (HUD grantees, lenders, Enterprises), legal practitioners, fair housing advocates, and agency staff preparing or responding to Federal Register rulemakings on fair housing
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing, submitting, or analyzing public comments and regulatory documents related to federal fair housing rulemakings and notices (HUD, FHFA, OCC, NCUA, etc.). Includes requirements for certifications, marketing plans, data collections, complaint forms, and procedural deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmatively Furthering Fair Housing - administration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with the Fair Housing Act, the Secretary requires that grantees administer all programs and activities related to housing and urban development in a manner to affirmatively further the policies of the Fair Housing Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each community receiving a grant under subpart D must submit a certification that it will affirmatively further fair housing, consistent with §§ 5.150 and 5.151. Program participants must continue to affirmatively further fair housing as and to the extent required by the Fair Housing Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency standard for AFFH certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantee AFFH certifications will be deemed sufficient provided they took any action during the relevant period rationally related to promoting fair housing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: actions 'rationally related to promoting fair housing, such as helping eliminate housing discrimination.' The interim final rule does not reinstate an obligation to conduct an Analysis of Impediments or mandate a specific planning mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmative Fair Housing Marketing Plan (AFHMP) submission and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for participation in FHA insurance or Multifamily Housing rental assistance programs must complete and submit an Affirmative Fair Housing Marketing plan form (AFHMP/HUD 935.2A/B/C) describing advertising and outreach activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AFHMP forms collect information on advertising and outreach activities of owners/developers to attract applicants/buyers that are least likely to apply due to race, color, national origin, religion, sex (including sexual orientation and gender identity), disability, or familial status; forms assist grantees and insured housing with compliance with the Fair Housing Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protected-classes coverage in marketing/outreach requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Affirmative marketing and outreach activities must consider and aim to attract individuals least likely to apply because of protected characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protected characteristics listed in notices: race, color, national origin, religion, sex (including sexual orientation and gender identity), disability, and familial status. AFHMP forms are used to document planned activities targeting those least likely to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for rescinding obsolete regulations (OCC part 27 example)
rubrics_metrics.description: A regulation may be rescinded if it is obsolete, duplicative of other legal authorities, inconsistent with other authorities, imposes asymmetrical burdens, or the data collected has limited utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCC rationale for rescission: part 27 was obsolete, largely duplicative and inconsistent with other legal authorities requiring data collection on home loan applications; it imposed asymmetrical data collection requirements and the data collected had limited utility; rescission should not materially impact availability of data necessary for supervisory activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with underlying statutory obligations despite regulatory repeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Repealing or rescinding an agency regulation does not relieve regulated entities of obligations under underlying statutes and other laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FHFA stated repeal of its part 1293 regulation 'does not change Enterprise or Bank obligations to meet statutory and regulatory affordable housing goals' and that entities must continue to comply with Fair Housing Act, ECOA, Safety and Soundness Act, and UDAP prohibitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disparate impact (discriminatory effects) administrative standard vs. court determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether HUD should maintain its administrative discriminatory effects regulations that formalize tests for unjustified discriminatory effect (disparate impact) or remove them and leave interpretation to the courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD's 2013 rules imposed a presumption of unlawful discrimination when variance in outcomes exists among protected classes even without intent; HUD proposed removing its discriminatory effects regulations so courts address disparate impact liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance document withdrawal affects agency interpretations
rubrics_metrics.description: Withdrawal of previously issued guidance documents changes the agency's nonbinding interpretive guidance and may affect enforcement and expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of withdrawn documents: 'Application of the Fair Housing Act to the Advertising of Housing, Credit, and Other Real Estate-Related Transactions through Digital Platforms'; FHEO memoranda on service/assistance animals and reasonable accommodation requests; notices on source of income testing activities. Withdrawal removes those interpretive references from FHEO guidance materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural fairness in comment periods (extensions and waivers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should provide fair opportunity for public comment, and may extend comment periods or grant waivers to standard timing requirements when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD extended a comment period seven days due to a technical problem with regulations.gov that impeded electronic submissions. Secretary (through Deputy Secretary) can waive minimum 30-day application periods for FHIP NOFOs when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information collection and PRA notice-and-comment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must publish notices of proposed information collection (PRA) and solicit public comment for the prescribed period (e.g., 60 days) prior to OMB approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: HUD's 60-day notice for the Housing Discrimination Complaint Form HUD-903 seeks comment on the proposed collection and explains the form's purpose and who may file under § 810(a) of the Fair Housing Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents and purpose of Housing Discrimination Complaint form (HUD-903)
rubrics_metrics.description: The HUD-903 form facilitates collection of pertinent information from persons or entities wishing to file housing discrimination complaints with HUD under § 810(a) of the Fair Housing Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by persons claiming injury by discriminatory housing practices or those who aided/encouraged another person to exercise fair housing rights; PRA notice solicits feedback on the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair housing testing pool inclusion policy
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD may permit FHIP and FHAP funded entities to use fair housing testers with prior felony convictions or convictions for fraud/perjury to better investigate discriminatory criminal background screening policies and to improve inclusivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rule eliminates restrictions barring testers with prior convictions, based on HUD's determination that no valid interest is served by a categorical bar and to ensure adequate investigation of potentially discriminatory policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory accuracy and currency requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency regulations should be up-to-date and reflect current statutory interpretation, case law, and regulatory developments; outdated or redundant agency regulations risk causing confusion or unnecessary burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NCUA proposed removing a nondiscrimination regulation because its last substantive amendment was in 2001 and it may not reflect subsequent case law or regulatory developments under the FHA; agencies should avoid redundant summaries that conflict with primary jurisdiction (e.g., HUD).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and evidentiary standards for equal access (sex/gender)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations may define protected characteristics (e.g., sex, gender identity) and set standards for eligibility and reasonable assurances/evidence when programs permit single-sex or sex-specific facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A proposed HUD rule would remove references to 'gender' and 'gender identity' or replace them with 'sex' as defined by an Executive Order; would permit grant recipients and program operators to require reasonable assurances and evidence to confirm an individual's sex to protect safety in single-sex facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: FHFA requirements for fair lending/fair housing oversight and plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulated entities may be required to comply with FHFA supervisory expectations, provide reports, maintain data systems, and adopt Equitable Housing Finance Plans to address barriers for underserved communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FHFA codified practices including orders for regular/special reports, guidance on supervisory expectations, coordination with HUD, fair lending oversight data systems, and referral programs for potential mortgage pricing discrimination.
